text:
alex: heads-up — new users hitting our onboarding sampleapp see sporadic SSE disconnects right after auth refresh. repro on JS + python sdks.
rita: ugh, do you have a minimal repro? can you paste logs? :thinking_face: 
alex: yeah. repro steps: open sampleapp, start streaming echo bot, wait ~65s for token refresh. sometimes client sees `xhr closed` then a bunch of duplicate final tokens. logs: 
```
[2026-03-20T12:01:05Z] stream: connected (sid=abc123)
[2026-03-20T12:02:10Z] auth: refresh start
[2026-03-20T12:02:11Z] stream: recv chunk id=45 "data:{...}"
[2026-03-20T12:02:11Z] stream: recv chunk id=46 "data:{...}"
[2026-03-20T12:02:11Z] stream: connection closed (code=1006)
[2026-03-20T12:02:11Z] client: reconnect attempt 1
[2026-03-20T12:02:11Z] stream: recv chunk id=46 "data:{...}" // duplicate after reconnect
```
rita: that duplicate final token after reconnect smells like race between auth refresh and resume token generation. we saw similar in go sdk but not identical.
sam: are both SDKs using the same `Last-Event-ID` semantics? iirc python sdk sets `Last-Event-ID` but js uses `?last_event_id=` param for sampleapp. could be parity mismatch.
maya: also worth checking whether our auth refresh handler aborts the inflight xhr vs letting it finish. if we abort and re-open, server might send final token twice if resume isn't atomic on server.
alex: confirmed: js sampleapp does `xhr.abort()` when refresh starts. python lets the connection finish and then reconnects. js flow is cleaner for latency but triggers duplicate payloads sometimes.
sam: ok that explains parity. which behavior do we want? let inflight finish (safer) or abort and re-establish (lower tail latency)?
rita: default to safe for sampleapp/onboarding — less noisy for new users. we can expose config for latency-sensitive users.
maya: quick patch: in js sdk, on auth refresh don't abort; instead set a header on the next reconnect and rely on server-side resume. also add dedupe on client for identical chunk ids for 5s window.
alex: do we have chunk ids guaranteed unique across reconnects? server adds `chunk_id` header to each SSE event. if not present we fallback to checksum.
sam: add note to SDK parity doc and update sampleapp readme. i'll open a tiny PR to change js sampleapp flow and add unit test simulating mid-refresh.
maya: also add telemetry flag for `sse_duplicate_after_refresh` to help quantify impact.
rita: can we surface a small hint in onboarding UX? e.g., "If stream disconnects briefly during auth refresh, it will resume automatically" — reduces support tickets. :thumbsup:
alex: yes. i'll make the js PR + sampleapp README update. sam, can you do the doc parity change?
sam: on it. will also add a small e2e test in CI that forces token refresh at 60s and asserts no duplicate final tokens.
deploy-bot: deployment queued: branch/js-sse-refresh-fix to staging (rollout: 5% -> 100%) — ETA 10m.
alex: awesome. follow-ups:
- add dedupe heuristic in SDKs (js/python)
- add sampleapp readme note
- add telemetry metric
- small UX blurb for onboarding

rita: thanks team. this should cut down the "stream spam" tickets.
alex: marking this thread resolved for now, will reopen if staging shows regressions. :white_check_mark:
